restrictions.area: on or within 100 yards of any primary or secondary highway
restrictions.exceptions: necessary crossing to enter or leave a lawful hunting area
restrictions.summary: You may not hunt with a firearm on or within 100 yards of a primary or secondary highway.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful to hunt or attempt to hunt with a firearm any game bird or game animal while the hunting or attempting to hunt is on or within one hundred (100) yards of any primary or secondary highway

restrictions.area: public property, including schools, parks, pools, courthouse and county offices
restrictions.summary: Shooting and hunting are prohibited on any public property.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful to shoot or hunt on any public property including, but not limited to, schools, parks, pools, the courthouse and other county offices.

restrictions.exceptions: law enforcement, military; persons needing it for safety in employment
restrictions.summary: It is illegal to have a loaded rifle or shotgun in a vehicle on any public road in the county.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to transport, possess or carry a loaded shotgun or loaded rifle in any vehicle on any public street, road or highway within county.

restrictions.exceptions: permission of owner or tenant
restrictions.summary: You may not shoot an arrow so that it can be expected to hit another person's property without permission.
restrictions.quote: No person shall discharge an arrow from any bow in a manner that can be reasonably expected to result in the impact of the arrow upon the property of another without permission

restrictions.area: shooting-prohibited areas (Sec. 26-18)
restrictions.exceptions: ranges; where firearms may be lawfully discharged; private property with permission
restrictions.summary: Pneumatic guns are restricted in the shooting-prohibited areas.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful to shoot pneumatic guns in the areas set forth in County Code section 26-18, except as provided below

conflicts: State firearm seasons apply countywide, but firearm discharge is banned in five large shooting-prohibited areas (Lake Arrowhead, Garrisonville, Aquia, South Stafford, Widewater), leaving archery only there.
notes: Sec. 26-17 lists no exceptions on this page (e.g. no acreage or deer-permit exception). Sec. 26-10's ban on shooting or hunting on 'any public property' could be read to include state or federal lands; the text names only county facilities as examples. Sec. 26-3 (street/public gathering) mirrors state law.

restrictions.exceptions: permanently disabled hunters (Va. Code 29.1-528.2); dispatching an animal wounded from the stand; landowner/lessee damage kills under 29.1-529
restrictions.summary: Deer and bear may be hunted with rifles .23 caliber or larger only from an elevated stand at least 10 feet high; chamber a round only on the stand or when going to a wounded animal.
restrictions.quote: The person shall hunt only from an elevated stand located at least ten feet above the ground

restrictions.area: from the road and within 10 feet of the ditch bank
restrictions.exceptions: necessary crossing of highways
restrictions.summary: No hunting with a firearm from a road or within 10 feet of the ditch bank.
restrictions.quote: It is unlawful to hunt with a firearm in the county from the road and within 10 feet of the ditch bank.

restrictions.area: Surry Landing on the James subdivision
restrictions.summary: No hunting with firearms or any other weapon in the Surry Landing on the James subdivision.
restrictions.quote: No person shall hunt with firearms or other weapons in the Surry Landing on the James subdivision

restrictions.area: within 100 yards of any property line of a public school or county park
restrictions.exceptions: lands within a national or state park or forest, or wildlife management area
restrictions.summary: No shooting a firearm or hunting within 100 yards of a public school or county park property line.
restrictions.quote: It is unlawful in the county for any person to shoot a firearm or to hunt within 100 yards of any property line of a public school or a county park.

restrictions.exceptions: with permission of the property owner
restrictions.summary: Bows may not be shot where the arrow can be expected to land on another's property without permission.
restrictions.quote: It is unlawful to discharge a bow and arrow in a manner that can be reasonably expected to result in the impact of the arrow upon the property of another without permission from the owner of such property.

conflicts: Statewide rules allow rifles from the ground; Surry requires a 10-ft elevated stand for deer and bear rifles .23 caliber or larger.
notes: No weapon type is removed; rifles remain usable for deer/bear from elevated stands, and .22+ rifles for other game (including turkey) per state law. Sec. 20-101 'or to hunt' within 100 yards appears to cover all weapons, though weapons recorded as all_firearms for the shooting clause.

restrictions.exceptions: disabled hunter exemption from the stand requirement (Va. Code 29.1-528.2); landowner/lessee damage kills under 29.1-529
restrictions.summary: Deer may be hunted with non-muzzleloading rifles only if .23 caliber or larger, from an elevated stand at least 10 feet high, with written landowner permission, chambering a round only on the stand.
restrictions.quote: a person may use a rifle other than a muzzle-loading rifle to hunt deer during the regular hunting season only as follows: (1)The rifle shall be a 0.23 caliber or larger; (2)The person shall hunt only from an elevated stand at least ten feet

restrictions.summary: No rifle of any type, including muzzleloading rifles, may be used to hunt wild turkey.
restrictions.quote: No rifle of any type may be used to hunt or take wild turkey.

restrictions.summary: Written landowner permission is required to hunt deer with a rifle (and, per Sec. 4-157(d), apparently with a muzzleloader).
restrictions.quote: The person first obtains written permission from the landowner.

restrictions.summary: Muzzleloading rifles for deer must be single-shot and .45 caliber or larger; modern scoped muzzleloaders are legal.
restrictions.quote: Rifles shall be .45 caliber or larger, and handguns shall be .40 caliber or larger, and modern muzzle loading rifles, which may include telescopic sights.

conflicts: Statewide rules allow centerfire rifles for deer from the ground and rifles for turkey; Sussex requires deer rifles to be .23+ caliber and used only from a 10-foot elevated stand with written landowner permission, and bans all rifles for turkey.
notes: Sec. 4-158 is internally contradictory (no scopes/sabots vs. modern scoped muzzleloaders allowed); DWR's note says modern scoped muzzleloaders are legal. Slug guns may be used without the elevated stand (4-160(c)). Bear is not addressed. Sec. 4-157(d) written-permission clause placement is ambiguous.

restrictions.area: public parks, parkways, and county lands used for related purposes
restrictions.exceptions: written consent of administrator; law enforcement; concealed handgun permit holders (carry only)
restrictions.summary: Carrying or discharging firearms and killing or disturbing animals in county parks is prohibited without the administrator's written consent.
restrictions.quote: To carry or discharge any firearms, firecrackers, rockets, torpedoes or fireworks of any kind without written consent of the administrator

restrictions.summary: Killing coyotes is permitted countywide, and the county pays a bounty for coyotes killed on agricultural land.
restrictions.quote: the killing of coyotes within the boundaries of the County of Tazewell shall be permitted

notes: Coyote bounty is permissive and does not restrict weapons. Remaining park rules (fishing, camping, etc.) omitted as unrelated.

restrictions.area: designated subdivisions/areas: Skyland Estates, Apple Mountain Lake, Shenandoah Farms (and listed adjacent parcels), Shenandoah Shores, Lake Front Royal, Apple Mountain Lake South, High Knob, Stonewall Estates subdivisions; and the South Fork of the Shenandoah River from the Route 619 bridge to the confluence with the North Fork
restrictions.exceptions: bowhunting by a property owner on his own property in such subdivision at least 100 yards from residences and roads
restrictions.summary: All hunting with firearms or other weapons, including bows, is prohibited in the listed subdivisions and on the specified stretch of the South Fork Shenandoah River; owners may bowhunt their own land if at least 100 yards from residences and roads.
restrictions.quote: all hunting with firearms or other weapons, including bow and arrow, is prohibited in the following designated subdivisions or other areas of the County

restrictions.summary: No loaded rifle or shotgun may be carried in a vehicle on any public road in the county.
restrictions.quote: unlawful for any person to transport, possess or carry a loaded shotgun or loaded rifle in any vehicle on any public street, road or highway within Warren County

conflicts: In the listed subdivisions (e.g., Shenandoah Farms, Skyland Estates, High Knob) state seasons do not apply: no firearm hunting at all, and archery only by owners on their own land 100+ yards from residences and roads.
notes: These no-hunting subdivisions are named, signed areas (some large, e.g., Shenandoah Farms) that could be mapped as polygons using Warren County tax maps; affects_hunting_map set false because they are scattered subdivisions rather than the whole county, but the caller may want to treat them as mappable no-firearm zones.
No hunting weapon or hunting restrictions on this page: only a kennel-dog licensing rule (dogs may be removed from kennels to hunt) and a zoning list allowing hunting preserves in the CR district.

restrictions.exceptions: may fire on ground to dispatch deer wounded from the stand
restrictions.summary: Rifles .23 caliber or larger may be used for deer only from a stand at least 8 feet high, with a magazine of 5 rounds or fewer and written landowner permission.
restrictions.quote: Rifles of .23 caliber or larger with a maximum magazine capacity of five rounds may be used to hunt deer during the firearms deer season provided the hunter is in an elevated stand at least eight feet above ground level

restrictions.exceptions: groundhogs and coyotes outside the general firearms deer season
restrictions.summary: Rifles larger than .22 are allowed for groundhogs and coyotes only outside the general firearms deer season; other big-game rifle use is not listed as allowed.
restrictions.quote: Rifles larger than .22 will be allowed to hunt groundhogs and coyotes outside of the general firearms deer season.

conflicts: Centerfire rifles for deer require an 8-ft elevated stand, 5-round maximum magazine and written landowner permission.
The ordinance lists only allowed rifle uses under § 29.1-528; rifles larger than .22 for bear or other game are not listed and may be prohibited.
notes: Sec. 30-2 is phrased as a list of allowed activities rather than prohibitions; the implied general rifle restriction is not stated in the text shown. Muzzleloaders are legal in any firearms season.

restrictions.exceptions: law enforcement/game wardens; military; zoned firing ranges; deer population control permit under Va. Code 29.1-529; defense or dangerous/destructive animals
restrictions.summary: Rifles larger than .22 rimfire may not be fired anywhere in York County, so centerfire rifles cannot be used for hunting.
restrictions.quote: No person shall discharge at any location in the county any rifle of a caliber larger than .22 rimfire

conflicts: State allows centerfire rifles for deer and bear; York County bans discharge of any rifle over .22 rimfire countywide, so deer hunters must use shotguns, muzzleloaders, or archery.
notes: Muzzleloading rifles over .22 caliber are technically rifles; the ordinance does not expressly exempt them, so muzzleloader rifles may also be barred (title says 'high-powered rifles'). Verify.

restrictions.exceptions: law enforcement; justifiable self-defense; otherwise specifically authorized by law; shotgun hunting permit under Sec 12-28 (and ATC 12-11.1)
restrictions.summary: Discharging any gun, pistol, rifle or other firearm anywhere in the town is prohibited.
restrictions.quote: any person who willfully discharges or causes to be discharged any gun, pistol, rifle or firearm of any type of description in the town, shall be guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor

restrictions.area: permitted parcels of at least 50 acres
restrictions.summary: The only firearm hunting allowed is with a shotgun loaded with multiple ball shot (no slugs) on a parcel of 50+ acres that holds a police-issued permit, with written owner permission and posted signs.
restrictions.quote: lawful for any person to hunt or attempt to hunt any game animal or game bird with a shotgun, when such shotgun is loaded with ammunition consisting of multiple ball shot, on land for which there has been issued to the fee owner or tenant thereof a permit

restrictions.summary: Where firearm hunting is allowed by permit, it is shotgun-with-shot only; rifles, pistols and muzzleloading rifles are not allowed.
restrictions.quote: with a shotgun, when such shotgun is loaded with ammunition consisting of multiple ball shot

restrictions.summary: Permitted shotgun hunting must use multiple ball shot (buckshot/shot), not slugs.
restrictions.quote: loaded with ammunition consisting of multiple ball shot

restrictions.summary: A shotgun hunting permit can only be issued for a parcel (or jointly acknowledged contiguous land) totaling at least 50 acres.
restrictions.quote: totals in area not less than fifty (50) acres

restrictions.area: within 200 yards of any structure, public school grounds, public park, public roadway or private road serving two or more residences
restrictions.summary: Even with a permit, no shotgun hunting or discharge within 200 yards of any structure, school, park, public road or shared private road.
restrictions.quote: No permit shall allow hunting or discharging of a shotgun within two hundred (200) yards of any structure or public school grounds, public park, public roadway or private road serving two (2) or more residences.

restrictions.exceptions: approved ranges; property where firearms may lawfully be discharged; private property with owner permission using reasonable care
restrictions.summary: Air/pellet/BB guns may only be shot at ranges, where firearms are lawful, or on private property with permission keeping projectiles on the property.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to shoot a pneumatic gun in the town, except at facilities approved for shooting ranges

conflicts: State firearms seasons (including muzzleloader and rifle) are effectively unavailable in the town: firearm discharge is banned except buckshot/shot shotgun hunting on permitted 50+ acre parcels; archery is not restricted by these ordinances.
notes: DWR labels this 'Ashland City' but it is the Town of Ashland. Sec 12-27 references an exception in ATC section 12-11.1, whose text is not on the page.

restrictions.exceptions: law enforcement; self-defense; special permit issued by the town on written application showing good cause
restrictions.summary: No gun, pistol or other firearm may be fired within the town or on town property without a town special permit.
restrictions.quote: No person shall fire or discharge any gun, pistol, or other firearm within the town or on town-owned property.

restrictions.summary: A special town permit, applied for in writing with good cause, is required to discharge a firearm.
restrictions.quote: By special permit issued by the town containing reasonable conditions or restrictions, upon written application showing good cause

conflicts: State firearm seasons do not apply in town limits without a special town permit.
notes: Sec. 16-1 is titled 'Air guns, slingshots, etc.' but its text (as reproduced by DWR) repeats the firearm discharge ban, so the actual air gun rule is unclear. Archery not addressed.

restrictions.exceptions: urgent necessity
restrictions.summary: Discharging any rifle, shotgun or firearm of any kind in the town is illegal except in urgent necessity.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge any rifle, shotgun or firearm of any description, except upon urgent necessity.

restrictions.exceptions: deer archery hunting under Sec. 42-21
restrictions.summary: Bows, crossbows, air guns and slingshots may not be discharged in town, except deer archery hunting under the town's rules.
restrictions.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge or use any slingshot, sling, gravel shooter, air gun, bow, crossbow or similar implement.

restrictions.dates: DWR archery seasons including early and late special urban archery seasons
restrictions.summary: Deer bowhunters must register with the Rocky Mount Police Department, provide written landowner permission, carry the registration form, and report deer taken, missed and wounded.
restrictions.quote: Any person engaged in the taking of deer with archery equipment inside the town boundaries shall register with the Town of Rocky Mount Police Department.

restrictions.summary: Deer archery must be from stands at least 10 feet above the surrounding land; not on school or church property.
restrictions.quote: The discharge of archery equipment for the taking of deer shall be from stands elevated not less than ten feet above the level of surrounding land.

restrictions.area: within 300 feet of any residence; within 100 feet of any highway, street, alley, roadway, sidewalk, or designated foot trail
restrictions.summary: No arrows within 300 feet of any residence or 100 feet of any road, sidewalk or designated foot trail.
restrictions.quote: The discharge of archery equipment shall not occur closer than 300 linear feet from any residence.

restrictions.summary: Firearms of any type may not be used or carried while deer hunting in town.
restrictions.quote: Firearms of any type, caliber or description, shall not be used or carried during deer hunting.

conflicts: State firearm, muzzleloader, bear and turkey seasons cannot be used in town: all firearm discharge is banned; only deer archery with police registration is allowed.
notes: DWR labels this page 'Rocky Mount City'; it is the Town of Rocky Mount. Sec. 42-17 text does not say 'within the town' but is a town ordinance applying within town limits. Sec. 42-21(e) references 42-18's prohibitions remaining in effect.
